assertion: The Community College System of New Hampshire rose from 23,325 to 24,741, up 6.1%, a level the brief describes as the highest since at least 2001-02.
It counts 9,364 high school students taking community college courses for credit in 2024-25, up from 7,585 two years earlier. They were 37.8% of the system's enrollment.
Subtract them, by GSR's arithmetic, and 15,377 students remain.
New Hampshire's public colleges and universities enrolled 56,395 students in 2014-15 and 51,100 in 2024-25, a 9.4% decline.
The University System of New Hampshire fell from 33,070 students to 26,359, down 20.3%.
The number of New Hampshire high school graduates fell 4.8% from 2014 to 2024. The number who enrolled in college fell 15.6%. The share going straight to college dropped from 60.9% to 53.9%.
Average tuition and required fees for a full-time undergraduate at a university system school were $14,435 in 2024-25, down 17.6% after inflation from 2019-20.

sql: SELECT i.inst_name, f."year", f.eftotlt FROM edu.ipeds_fall_enrollment f JOIN edu.ipeds_institutions i ON i.unitid=f.unitid AND i."year"=f."year" WHERE f.efalevel=1 AND f."year" IN (2014,2023) AND i.state_abbr='NH' AND i.inst_name ILIKE '%Community College%'
